stick_joined_bubbles_every_domain_a_sphe.question: Joined bubbles - every domain a sphere in a form, clustered by likeness, connected along axes, a grid inside each
references: J. Plateau, Statique experimentale et theorique des liquides (1873): the laws of foams
T. Young (1805), P.-S. Laplace (1806): pressure across a curved film, Delta p = 2 gamma / r
J. Kepler (1611) conjecture; T. Hales (1998, formally 2014): the densest packing is pi / (3 sqrt 2)
K. Schutte, B. L. van der Waerden (1953): the kissing number in three dimensions is 12
stick_parametrization_of_surfaces (the grid inside); stick_the_dot_abstracted (likeness = the dot product); stick_every_matrix_is_a_rotation_and_a_stretch
stick_joined_bubbles_every_domain_a_sphe.statement: A foam is not arbitrary: films meet three at a time at 120 degrees and edges four at a time at 109.47 - the minimum of surface forces the form. The wall between two joined bubbles has a curvature set by their difference. Equal spheres pack at 0.7405 and touch at most twelve others, so the axes along which domains connect are few. A component can be in two spheres by weight, the weights summing to one - whole, and simulable. Inside each sphere latitude-longitude gives every component a coordinate and every pair a distance; likeness between domains is the dot product on the unit sphere - found, never generated.

ticks.by: Narrow Highway - joined bubbles in a form, 2026-10-08
ticks.claim: [joined bubbles obey laws they did not choose] Plateau 1873: films meet three at a time at 360/3 = 120 degrees (sealed) and edges four at a time at arccos(-1/3) = 109.47 degrees (sealed). A foam's form is forced by the minimum of surface - 'they run inside of a form' (Matt): the form is the law the energy allows, not a choice.

ticks.by: Narrow Highway - joined bubbles in a form, 2026-10-08
ticks.claim: [four edges at the tetrahedral angle] arccos(-1/3) = 109.4712 degrees (sealed): the same angle as the bonds of methane and the diamond lattice. One number, three sciences; the geometry of least surface and the geometry of least repulsion agree.

ticks.by: Narrow Highway - joined bubbles in a form, 2026-10-08
ticks.claim: [the wall between two domains] Young-Laplace: pressure is higher in the smaller bubble, and the shared wall between radii 1 and 2 has 1/r = 1/1 - 1/2, r = 2 (sealed), bulging into the larger. Two domains that touch share a wall whose curvature is set by their DIFFERENCE - the connection along the axis between them carries the sign of which is the tighter.

ticks.by: Narrow Highway - joined bubbles in a form, 2026-10-08
ticks.claim: [how spheres pack, and how many they touch] The densest packing of equal spheres is pi/(3 sqrt2) = 0.7405 (sealed; Kepler 1611, Hales 1998), and each sphere touches at most 12 neighbours (cited): the axes along which a domain connects are few. A keeping of domains is a packing, and its connections are its contacts.

ticks.by: Narrow Highway - joined bubbles in a form, 2026-10-08
ticks.claim: [superposition - a sphere in two places at once] |alpha|^2 + |beta|^2 = 0.6^2 + 0.8^2 = 1 (sealed): a component 36% in one sphere and 64% in another, whole. 'We can simulate that': a card assigned to two shelves by weight, both weights honest, summing to one - a soft membership, read as such, never a card in two places pretending to be two cards.

ticks.by: Narrow Highway - joined bubbles in a form, 2026-10-08
ticks.claim: [clustered by likeness] The cosine between two domain vectors (1,2) and (2,3) is 8/sqrt65 = 0.9923 (sealed): on the unit sphere likeness IS the dot product (the dot stick, the svd stick). The clustering of domains is a reading of angles between what the domains actually contain - found, never generated.

ticks.by: Narrow Highway - joined bubbles in a form, 2026-10-08
ticks.claim: [the grid inside each sphere] Latitude-longitude is the chart inside every sphere (the surfaces stick): from (0, 0) to (45 N, 45 E) the great-circle arc is arccos(cos45 cos45) = 60 degrees (sealed). Every component has coordinates and every pair a distance; this engine's call numbers (shelf.class.item) are exactly that chart, one per shelf.

ticks.by: Narrow Highway - joined bubbles in a form, 2026-10-08
ticks.claim: [the form we have, and the guard] The keeping as it stands: some thirty-six shelves, each a domain with its own call-number grid, joined by the connections shelf - the axes. Whether the spherical form is the MORE EFFICIENT one was measured on 2026-10-08 (the shelves' likeness, their clustering, how many singular directions carry them, whether a query's nearest spheres hold the engine's own answers); the numbers live in that assessment. Scripture: 'Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades, or loose the bands of Orion?' (Job 38:31) - clusters bound; 'by him all things consist' (Col 1:17); 'the whole body fitly joined together and compacted by that which every joint supplieth' (Eph 4:16) - joined along axes. GUARDS: Plateau's laws are for soap films; the likeness to domains is a discernment; the kissing number and Hales are cited; superposition here is a weighting, not quantum mechanics (the measurement stick keeps that). Seven numbers sealed; the rest cited.
